subject.title: Bounded memory tool with hard character limits

question: Should OpenClaw define a first-class bounded memory write/CRUD contract in memory-core, and what limit, identity, duplicate/consolidation, snapshot, config, and secret-handling semantics should it expose?
rationale: Current main has only read/recall memory tools plus partial safeguards, and choosing a durable memory-write API changes product behavior, plugin surface, security posture, and user expectations.

options.title: Define bounded memory-core CRUD
options.body: Make memory-core the canonical owner for bounded add/list/replace/remove behavior with hard limits and security-aware storage semantics.

options.title: Limit scope to partial safeguards
options.body: Keep improving flush bounds, MEMORY.md budget warnings, and UI warnings without adding a general write/CRUD API yet.

options.title: Prototype outside default memory-core
options.body: Explore the CRUD contract as an external plugin or ClawHub path first, then promote only if the API proves stable.

recommendation.title: Define bounded memory-core CRUD
recommendation.body: Make memory-core the canonical owner for bounded add/list/replace/remove behavior with hard limits and security-aware storage semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice spans product direction, API exposure, security posture, and core/plugin boundaries, which matches the BDFL/product-decision role identified in CONTRIBUTING.md.
